purpose: Convert evidence-supported ingredient amounts into feasible product schedules without assuming clinical equivalence.
hard_rules: Arithmetic equivalence is descriptive only until a schedule has evidence-supported status.
If the evidence-supported pattern is daily, prefer a product/form that can deliver the supported daily amount rather than concentrating doses on fewer days.
A tablet can be fractionated only when the manufacturer/formulation permits splitting.
Capsules and softgels are not treated as divisible.
Powders and liquids can support fractional amounts only when they can be measured with adequate accuracy.
If no feasible evidence-supported schedule matches the product, Vitami should recommend changing product strength/form rather than inventing a schedule.
Treatment regimens requiring diagnosis/laboratory follow-up remain professional-only.

example_logic.vitami_result: No automatic schedule: softgel is not assumed divisible and generic alternate-day clinical equivalence is not established. Prefer a lower-strength product if a validated 500 mg/day target exists for the indication.
Measure approximately 3 g daily if the product allows accurate measurement. Do not substitute 6 g every other day merely because the weekly average matches.
Calculate the evidence-based mg/kg range only after body weight, baseline caffeine, sleep and safety checks; schedule remains tied to the event rather than daily averaging.
Alternate-day schedules may be scientifically relevant in diagnosed iron-depletion/iron-deficiency contexts, but remain professional-only and are not derived by halving a daily target.
